items.summary: Mumbai-based Wockhardt has struck success in its innovative research on a range of antibiotic drugs, bridging a global pipeline gap for difficult-to-treat infections. In May this year, the company secured approvals from Indian and US drug regulators for a breakthrough drug, Zaynich (cefepime + zidebactam), to treat complicated urinary tract infection, including acute pyelonephritis or severe kidney infections. Wockhardt has showcased six drugs to treat antimicrobial resistance (AMR).

items.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed the Union government's appeal concerning disputes involving $99 million arbitral awards. Vedanta and Ravva Oil sought the enforcement of these awards related to the Ravva oilfield. The Delhi High Court had previously rejected the government's objections to enforcing the awards. The disputes originated from a 1994 production sharing contract between the petroleum ministry and various companies.

items.title: India Coal Imports Fall 5.8%, but Imported-Coal Plants Buy More
Coal India's October coal output rises 19.3% to 67.2 million tonnes
items.summary:
Coal India Ltd (CIL) on Sunday said its coal production rose 19.3 per cent year-on-year to 67.2 million tonnes (MT) in October.
The state-owned miner had produced 56.4 MT in the same month last year, according to provisional data filed with the stock exchanges.
Offtake in October stood at 70.3 MT, up 18.7 per cent from 59.2 MT a year ago.
For the April-October period of 2026-27, CIL's production inched up 0.7 per cent to 388.2 MT from 385.5 MT in the year-ago period. Offtake during the seven months grew 9.2 per cent to 454.6 MT from 416.2 MT.
Among the subsidiaries, Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd (MCL) recorded the highest production in October at 20.8 MT, up 25.3 per cent. South Eastern Coalfields Ltd (SECL) produced 14.3 MT, a rise of 17.4 per cent.
Western Coalfields Ltd (WCL) posted the sharpest growth, with output rising 64.7 per cent to 5.9 MT. Eastern Coalfields Ltd (ECL) produced 4.6 MT, up 27.9 per cent, while Central Coalfields Ltd (CCL) output rose 26.1 per cent to 7.3 MT.

items.summary:
Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd on Sunday said its total vehicle sales grew 9 per cent year-on-year to a record 13,1109 units in October.
The total sales include exports, which rose 77 per cent to 7,102 units during the month.
Mahindra & Mahindra said domestic passenger vehicle sales rose 2 per cent year-on-year to 73,338 units in October, and commercial vehicle sales rose 4 per cent to 33,037 units.
M&M Automotive business President Velusamy R said the company's SUV sales of 73,338 units and total vehicle sales of 13,1109 units in October were the highest ever in any month.
The festive season, together with a refreshed portfolio, kept demand strong across SUVs, pick-ups and three-wheelers. Our first CNG vehicle, the XUV 3XO ZNG, has also seen strong traction with customers, he said.
In commercial vehicles, three-wheeler sales, including electric ones, increased 38 per cent to 17,632 units. LCVs between 2-3.5 ton grew 5 per cent to 28,654 units, while sales of LCVs under 2 ton ...

items.summary:
Central Depository Services (India) Ltd (CDSL) reported a 24 per cent year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 173 crore for the July-September quarter, aided by continued growth in India's securities market participation.
Consolidated total income rose 22 per cent to Rs 417 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 341 crore a year earlier. Sequentially, net profit jumped 47 per cent from Rs 118 crore in the June quarter, while total income increased 22 per cent from Rs 341 crore.
For the first half of FY27, consolidated net profit grew 20 per cent to Rs 291 crore, while total income rose 19 per cent to Rs 758 crore.
On a standalone basis, CDSL's net profit increased 28 per cent year-on-year to Rs 163 crore in Q2, while total income rose 24 per cent to Rs 359 crore. For the six months ended September, standalone profit grew 10 per cent to Rs 308 crore and income increased 14 per cent to Rs 685 crore.

items.summary:
The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) invalidated a series of transactions involving JLS Realty Pvt Ltd, including the transfer of a prime redevelopment land parcel in Mumbai to Spenta Suncity and a mortgage and corporate guarantee linked to Rs 525 crore in financing involving IIFL.
In an order pronounced on October 23, the Mumbai bench of the tribunal also invalidated the appointment of two IIFL-linked employees as directors, declared the attempted removal of an existing director illegal, reversed disputed share transfers and ordered restoration of the company's land.
The Bench, comprising Judicial Member K R Saji Kumar and Technical Member Anil Raj Chellan, held that the sequence of events was "demonstrative of a deliberate design", constituting oppression marked by a "lack of probity and fair dealing".
The ruling follows five years of litigation initiated by Moniveda Consultants LLP and Rajat Jhunjhunwala against Shajas Developers, JLS Realty, and other respondents.
